title: Smoky Baba Ghanoush with Charred Aubergine, Tahini and Lemon
summary: Whole aubergines are charred until completely soft, drained, chopped and whisked into a lemon-garlic base with tahini, a little yoghurt and olive oil.
equipment: grill or gas hob, or an oven with a grill

ingredients.item: garlic cloves, grated to a paste
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Char the aubergines
steps.text: Prick each aubergine 6 times. Grill on a foil-lined tray as close to a very hot grill as possible, or turn over a gas flame or barbecue, for 30-40 minutes, turning every 10 minutes, until blackened and completely soft.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Put the aubergines in a colander and leave for 20 minutes to cool and drain off the bitter juices.

steps.title: Mellow the garlic
steps.text: Meanwhile stir the lemon juice, garlic and salt together in the bowl.

steps.title: Chop
steps.text: Split the aubergines, scoop out the flesh and discard the skin and stems. Chop the flesh finely and add it to the bowl.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Whisk in the tahini, yoghurt and 2 tbsp oil. Leave 20 minutes for the flavours to blend, then add more lemon to taste.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spread in a shallow bowl, drizzle with the remaining oil and scatter with parsley. Serve with warm pita.

tips: The blacker the skin, the smokier the dip; a gas flame or barbecue gives the most flavour.
Draining the flesh keeps the dip thick and stops it tasting bitter.
Chopping by hand gives a better texture than a food processor.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 4 days. Do not leave out for more than 2 hours. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
